title: Durable pre-activation source for approval riskTier and a run-linked applicablePolicyRef
description:
FILED BY architect-a69740e0 on 2026-08-28 at governor-0af24e35's explicit 17:59Z request ("both need a row FILED INTO PLANNING, and I do not create rows"). Measured independently at HEAD 3c23339a.

WHAT IT GATES: task-6646f888a488481e936dc0dd3f966cd5 (P2.15d-i, the daemon-owned approval intent seam), which is in PLANNING now and WILL re-block the moment a worker reaches the step that needs an honest riskTier and policy ref. Filing it before that happens rather than after.

THE GAP, MEASURED. An `ApprovalDecisionRecord` carries `riskTier` (packages/core/src/policy/approval-contract.ts:58, typed `PolicyRiskTier`) and `applicablePolicyRef` (a 64-hex ref). Excluding tests and fixtures, at HEAD:
- `riskTier` PRODUCERS are exactly TWO, and both are hardcoded constants for one path each: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/demo-seed-payloads.ts:406` writes the literal `"R2"` (a SEED, not production authority) and `apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion-authority.ts:70` writes the literal `"R3"` for the recovery journey only. Everything else is a CONSUMER: policy-risk-leg.ts:69/:83 reads it, recovery-completion.ts:123 compares it, expansion-approval.ts:226 and expansion-preparation.ts:84/:141/:243 validate it, approval-invalidation.ts:73 branches on R3. So a PRE-ACTIVATION approval on the ordinary plan path has NO durable source for its tier.
- `applicablePolicyRef` PRODUCERS are exactly ONE: `demo-seed-payloads.ts:390` writes `hex64("aa")`, again a seed constant. The real CONSUMERS compare it against a durable value that does exist elsewhere — `graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:86` against `predecessor.boundHashes.policyHash`, and `recovery-completion.ts:127`/`:161` against `found.evidence.policyRevisionRef`. So the NOTION of a durable policy ref exists; what is missing is a run-linked one produced at approval time.

WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A DEFAULT. The governor stated the prohibition plainly: "do not invent a default riskTier, do not synthesize a policy ref to get green." A tier decides whether step-up human authority is required (approval-invalidation.ts:73 special-cases R3), so a defaulted tier silently decides an authority question. A synthesized policy ref would make `applicablePolicyRef` comparisons pass against a value nothing durably asserted, which is the same class of fabrication the supersede binding row exists to prevent. Absence and a defaulted value are different answers and must stay different: if no durable tier or ref is available for a given run, the honest outcome is a REFUSAL with a stable code, not a fallback.

SCOPE. Land the durable pre-activation SOURCE — where a run's risk tier and its applicable policy ref are decided, recorded and read back — such that an approval record composed for a plan approval carries values read from the store rather than chosen by a caller or defaulted by the daemon. NOT IN SCOPE: task-6646f888's approval-intent seam itself (it consumes this), the supersede binding (task-b54b5609), or the recovery journey's existing R3 path, which already has its own durable evidence and must not be disturbed.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST: the two existing consumers already name durable values of the right shape — `boundHashes.policyHash` on the graph revision and `evidence.policyRevisionRef` on the recovery record. Measure whether one of those is the right source for the plan path before inventing a third notion; a third policy-ref concept that agrees with the other two today will drift tomorrow.

OWNERSHIP AT FILING: re-measure at claim. Probe with `git grep <pat> HEAD -- <paths>` or `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>`, never `git log --oneline -1 -- <path>` (prints nothing, EXITS 0 on an untracked path). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` immediately before the gate and quote it beside every grep; HEAD moves several times an hour here.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a row comment (the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every probe, each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control. Confirm the gap holds: excluding tests and fixtures, `riskTier` still has no production producer beyond demo-seed-payloads.ts:406 and recovery-completion-authority.ts:70, and `applicablePolicyRef` still has none beyond demo-seed-payloads.ts:390. If a durable source now exists, ADOPT it and report blocked as duplicate rather than building a second one.

A DURABLE, SERVER-DERIVED source for the run's risk tier exists and is read back from the store by production code — not defaulted, not caller-supplied, not seeded. A caller presenting its own riskTier is REFUSED with an exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer, both asserted, since more than one layer can refuse a bad approval.

The `applicablePolicyRef` an approval carries is RUN-LINKED and read from durable state, and it is the SAME notion the existing consumers already compare against rather than a third concept — measure `boundHashes.policyHash` (graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:86) and `evidence.policyRevisionRef` (recovery-completion.ts:127/:161) first and state in a row comment which one this path uses and why. A third policy-ref notion that agrees today drifts tomorrow.

ABSENCE REFUSES, IT DOES NOT DEFAULT. When no durable tier or policy ref is available for a run, the path returns a refusal naming which fact was unavailable, with its exact code and layer — never a fallback tier and never a synthesized ref. A mutation that substitutes a default for the refusal must red a NAMED arm, and a mutation that substitutes a different default must red the same arm (absence and a defaulted value are different answers).

The recovery journey's existing R3 path (recovery-completion-authority.ts:70, recovery-completion.ts:123/:127/:161) is UNCHANGED and its arms stay green, proven by running its suite unedited. This row adds a source for the plan path; it does not disturb a journey that already has durable evidence.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: name task-6646f888a488481e936dc0dd3f966cd5 as the consumer and record its id in a row comment, and prefer landing one durable call site so the source is composed rather than merely exported — a producer nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

Gates standalone, foreground and unpiped with nonzero counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, and the focused daemon suites quoting their `Test Files`/`Tests` count lines — the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus HEAD with an EMPTY owned-path intersection; every production file under 400 lines; every new `.ts` with its `.js` bridge; explicit-pathspec commit.
taskRails: Never invent a default riskTier and never synthesize an applicablePolicyRef to get green. The tier decides whether step-up human authority is required (approval-invalidation.ts:73 special-cases R3), so a defaulted tier silently decides an authority question; a synthesized ref makes comparisons pass against a value nothing durably asserted. Absence refuses with a stable code — it does not fall back.

Do not introduce a THIRD policy-ref notion. Two durable ones already exist and are compared by production consumers: `boundHashes.policyHash` and `evidence.policyRevisionRef`. Measure whether one of them is the right source for the plan path and say which; a third concept that agrees today drifts tomorrow.
Do not disturb the recovery journey's existing R3 path — it already has durable evidence and its arms must stay green, run unedited, as the proof.
This row lands the durable source. It does NOT plan, narrow or satisfy task-6646f888's approval-intent seam; that row consumes this one and certifies its own boundary.

CONFIRM THE GAP STILL HOLDS, excluding tests and fixtures:
- `riskTier` production producers are still only `demo-seed-payloads.ts:406` (literal "R2", a SEED) and `recovery-completion-authority.ts:70` (literal "R3", recovery journey only).
- `applicablePolicyRef` production producers are still only `demo-seed-payloads.ts:390` (`hex64("aa")`, a seed constant).

I ALREADY MEASURED THE THREE FACTS THAT SHAPE THIS ROW — verify each, do not re-derive:
(a) THE TIER IS ALREADY DURABLY RECORDED. `bootstrap-policy-services.ts` evaluates via `evaluatePolicy` and COMMITS through `commitAccepted(store, request, {aggregateId, …})` with `authoritativeRecord = {...evaluated.record, decisionDigest}`. `evaluatePolicy`'s returned `PolicyDecisionRecord` carries `riskAssessment: risk.assessment` AND `policyRevisionRef` (packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts:184-204).
(b) THE READER ALREADY RECOMPUTES IT AND THEN DROPS IT. `readPolicyEvaluationAuthority` (bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:115) calls `evaluatedOutcome(input)`, which re-runs `evaluatePolicy` and is verified against the stored digest — so the assessment is computed and checked inside the reader. But the returned `PolicyEvaluationAuthority` interface (:35-47) projects only action, decision, decisionDigest, decisionDigestVersion, graphNodeRevisionRefs, ok, policyRef, principalId, projectId, scope, sliceRef. NO tier. THAT omission is the riskTier half of this row.
(c) IT IS NOT RUN-LINKED. `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:61/:103) keys the decision to the project-scoped policy aggregate, and `policyRevisionRef` enters that evaluation as `input["policyRevisionRef"]` — CALLER-SUPPLIED. So neither half is run-linked today.

IF a durable run-linked source has since landed, ADOPT it and report blocked as duplicate rather than building a second one.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — DECIDE AND RECORD WHICH POLICY-REF NOTION THIS PATH USES. Read-only analysis, recorded in a row comment BEFORE any edit. Discharges DoD 3 and task rail 2.

Task rail 2 forbids a third policy-ref notion. Measure the two that exist and state which this path uses and why:
- `boundHashes.policyHash` on the graph revision, compared at `graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:86`.
- `evidence.policyRevisionRef` on the recovery record, compared at `recovery-completion.ts:127`/`:161`.

ARCHITECT'S MEASURED FINDING, verify it: `boundHashes` CANNOT be the pre-activation source. `graph-revision-reducer.ts:90` and `graph-revision-replay.ts:129` set `boundHashes: null` at creation and it is populated ONLY at the APPROVED transition (`:156`). At plan-review time it is null. That is precisely the trap this row exists to avoid, and it is why "read the activation witness's policyHash" is wrong.

BUT THE NOTION BEHIND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE, AND IT IS ALREADY NAMED. `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-policy-digest.ts` defines it: `APPROVAL_POLICY_DIGEST_VERSION = "moe.graph.approve.policy.v1"` (:31), `approvalPolicyMaterial(…)` (:69) and `approvalPolicyHash(material)` (:86), documented at :7 as "a digest over the policy decision that authorised THIS approval". `graph-transition-legs.ts:78` computes exactly that and feeds it in as `policyHash` (:92) — i.e. `boundHashes.policyHash` IS an `approvalPolicyHash`, just materialised later.

SO THE HONEST ANSWER, which you must confirm rather than assume: the pre-activation run-linked ref is the SAME `approvalPolicyHash` over the SAME material, computed at plan-review time from the run's durable policy authority instead of at transition time. That is ONE notion with two materialisation points, not a third concept — and it gives a checkable invariant: the value this row produces for a run must EQUAL the `boundHashes.policyHash` later written for that run's approval. State that invariant in the comment; step 5 asserts it.
If your measurement contradicts this, STOP and report rather than inventing a third ref.

STEP 3 — PROJECT THE TIER THROUGH THE AUTHORITY READER. Smallest honest change: surface a fact the reader already computes and already verifies. Invent no new authority.

In `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts`, widen the returned `PolicyEvaluationAuthority` (:35-47) to carry the replayed risk assessment's effective tier, taken from the SAME `evaluatedOutcome(input)` replay the reader already performs and already digest-verifies. Do not read it from the stored row unverified, and do not recompute it a second way.

BLAST-RADIUS CHECK FIRST, and this is load-bearing: `readPolicyEvaluationAuthority` has three production consumers — `activation/policy-admission-reader.ts`, `bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts`, and `bootstrap/bootstrap-services.test.ts`. Widening a RETURN type is additive, but an `exactObject`-style or exact-key assertion over the RETURNED object would break. `git grep -n 'readPolicyEvaluationAuthority' HEAD -- apps packages` and inspect each call site for exact-shape checks BEFORE editing. If one exists outside this row's roster, that is a split signal — STOP and report, do not take an extra path.
Do NOT change `ROW_KEYS` or `MATERIAL_KEYS`: those describe the STORED row and its material, which are unchanged by this row. If you find yourself editing either, you have changed the persisted shape rather than the projection — stop and re-read.

ABSENCE REFUSES. When the replay yields no groundable tier, the reader must REFUSE with a stable code at its existing `DAEMON_POLICY_AUTHORITY` layer — never project a fallback. `evaluatePolicy` already models this: `policy-evaluation.ts:51` states "No tier-bearing fact at all leaves computedTier null — never a silent R0", `:59-60` grounds a tier only on a fact clearing the strong-truth floor, `:175` emits `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE` and `:180` folds the decision to HOLD_UNKNOWN. Propagate that; do not soften it.

STEP 4 — THE RUN-LINKED PRE-ACTIVATION SOURCE. New module `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-risk-authority.ts` (<=250 lines, hard cap 400) plus its one-line bridge `approval-risk-authority.js` containing exactly `export * from "./approval-risk-authority.ts";` — the js-bridge rule: tsc and vitest resolve without it, plain Node does not.

It sits beside its neighbours by design: `approval-run-binding.ts` already binds an approval to a run, and `approval-policy-digest.ts` already owns the ref notion. Read both before writing; prefer composing them over duplicating either.

THE SEAM: given a runId (and the project), read the run's durable policy authority through step 3's widened reader and return BOTH facts for that run — the effective risk tier, and the `approvalPolicyHash` computed over `approvalPolicyMaterial(…)` per step 2's decision. Everything server-derived; nothing caller-supplied.
REFUSALS, each with an EXACT stable code AND the refusing layer, both asserted by the arms:
- No durable policy authority for the run -> refuse naming which fact was unavailable.
- Authority present but the tier is not groundable -> refuse carrying the unclassifiable code.
- A CALLER-PRESENTED riskTier or policy ref -> REFUSED (DoD 2 requires this explicitly). The seam takes a runId, not a tier; make presenting one structurally impossible in the signature where you can, and refused with a named code where you cannot.
Never return a fallback tier and never synthesize a ref. Absence and a defaulted value are DIFFERENT ANSWERS and must stay different — step 5's drills prove it.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: this row lands the SOURCE; it does NOT implement task-6646f888's approval-intent seam. Per the rail's clause (a), NAME the consumer and record its id — `task-6646f888a488481e936dc0dd3f966cd5` — in a durable row comment, stating that it composes this source. A producer nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist, so if a call site can be landed honestly without reaching into 6646f888's scope, prefer that and say what you did.

STEP 5 — DRILLS AND THE RECOVERY-PATH PROOF. Discharges DoD 4 and DoD 5.

DRILL A — ABSENCE MUST NOT BECOME A DEFAULT (DoD 4's exact requirement, and it needs TWO mutations because the DoD asks for two): (1) substitute a default tier for the refusal -> a NAMED arm must red; (2) substitute a DIFFERENT default -> the SAME named arm must red. Name the arm in the comment. If either mutation stays green, absence and a defaulted value are not being distinguished and that is a FINDING to report and stop on, not a pass.
DRILL B — CALLER-PRESENTED TIER: feed a caller-supplied riskTier and require the refusal arm to red with its exact code AND layer. Assert the layer too: more than one layer can refuse a bad approval, and an arm that only checks "it refused" is one added fence away from vacuous.
DRILL C — THE REF IS ONE NOTION, NOT THREE (step 2's invariant): mutate the produced ref away from `approvalPolicyHash(approvalPolicyMaterial(…))` and require the arm asserting agreement with the approval-time `boundHashes.policyHash` materialisation to red. This is what stops a third concept drifting in later.
RESTORE PROTOCOL: `git status --porcelain` each mutated path BEFORE mutating. Tracked paths take `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The NEW module, its bridge and its test are untracked (`??`) until committed and `git diff` is BLIND to them — prove those restores by SHA256 against an out-of-tree %TEMP% backup suffixed with your worker id. Two empty hashes compare equal and print match:true, so assert both are 64 hex chars AND equal.

RECOVERY PATH UNTOUCHED (DoD 5): run the recovery suite UNEDITED and quote its counts — `recovery-completion-authority.ts:70` and `recovery-completion.ts:123/:127/:161` keep their existing R3 durable-evidence path. This row ADDS a source for the plan path; it must not disturb a journey that already has durable evidence. If any recovery arm reds, you have changed shared behaviour — stop and report.

STEP 6 — GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE RECORD, PATHSPEC COMMIT. Discharges DoD 7.

GATES — FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ONE PER CALL, each with exit code AND count line. A piped run reports the tail's exit code; an exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING and is UNVERIFIED.
LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc` echo as execution evidence.
LEG B: focused daemon suites — `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json` over bootstrap-policy-authority.test.ts, approval-risk-authority.test.ts, bootstrap-services.test.ts and the recovery suite — exit 0, quote `Test Files` AND `Tests` counts.
NOTE: the root vitest include has NO `apps/**`, so a bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests and proves nothing here. Never cite it as daemon coverage.
LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` graded by PATH ATTRIBUTION — failures at the merge-base vs at HEAD, delta intersected with this row's owned paths must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red VERBATIM.
KNOWN FOREIGN RED, do not chase: TS2353 `'subscriberId' does not exist in type 'EventStreamAccessConfig'` at daemon-command-edges.ts and daemon-store-dependencies.ts — a peer mid-refactor in `http/event-stream-access.ts`. Re-measure whether it is still present and attribute it.
SIZE: every production file <= 400 lines, the new module targeted <= 250; every new `.ts` has its `.js` bridge.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, each answered with a measurement or an explicit N/A: what happens when two policy slices are installed between the run's evaluation and its approval (does the ref still agree with the later boundHashes.policyHash, and if not what refuses); a run with no policy authority at all; a run whose authority row is legacy or partially widened (the reader already has codes for this — name them); whether the widened projection changed any existing consumer's behaviour; whether a caller can reach the tier through any other path; and whether the digest-verified replay can disagree with the stored row without refusing.

RECORD via moe.add_comment, under ~4500 chars each, SPLIT rather than truncate (comments cap at 5000 SILENTLY). Carry: step 1's probes with HEAD quoted; step 2's policy-ref decision and its stated invariant; the blast-radius call-site inspection from step 3; all drill outcomes with the arm each redded; the recovery-suite counts; every gate's exit and counts; the foreign-red disclosure; and `task-6646f888a488481e936dc0dd3f966cd5` named as the consumer.
COMMIT by explicit pathspec naming only this row's owned paths. NEVER `git add -A` — the worktree carries heavy foreign WIP including an untracked `apps/daemon/src/cutover/` directory, and a whole-tree commit would sweep it. No push, no PR comment.

reopenReason:
GOVERNOR RE-SPEC HANDOFF 12:22Z — THE PLAN ASSERTS A FALSE INVARIANT AND THE WORKER PROVED IT. Routing to PLANNING because a BLOCKED row cannot be claimed by an architect, and this needs an architect, not another worker attempt.

WHAT STEP 2 DEMANDED: state, and have DRILL C assert, that a PRE-ACTIVATION approvalPolicyHash EQUALS the boundHashes.policyHash later written for that run. Step 2 also said: "If your measurement contradicts this, STOP and report rather than inventing a third ref."

IT DOES CONTRADICT, AND THE REASON IS CAUSAL, NOT COSMETIC. Of approvalPolicyMaterial's nine members (approval-policy-digest.ts:69-82), TWO — authorityDelayMs (:41) and grantPrincipalId (:45) — ARE decideApprovalAuthority's VERDICT (approval-policy.ts:130-136). They are produced BY the decision. A hash computed before the decision cannot contain the decision's own output. The invariant is not merely unmet at HEAD; it is unmeetable by construction. Zero bytes authored. Evidence: comment-aba4dd47aaed42edb48e5c6bb70dcd37 (step 2) and comment-a824f5372bcc41cd8c5c5486ce5c5590 (step 1).

THE WORKER DID EXACTLY RIGHT. They measured, found the plan's premise false, refused to invent a third ref to paper over it, and stopped where instructed. A drill forced to pass against a causally impossible invariant would have been a fabricated proof — the precise class Rail 4 forbids.

ARCHITECT, RE-SPEC THE INVARIANT — do not delete the row. The underlying need is real: task-6646f888 requires an honest pre-activation source for ApprovalDecisionRecord.riskTier and a run-linked 64-hex applicablePolicyRef, and it will re-block without it. Directions worth measuring: (a) define the pre-activation ref over ONLY the seven members that exist before the decision, excluding authorityDelayMs and grantPrincipalId, and state that exclusion explicitly in the DoD so nobody re-adds them; or (b) keep all nine but bind the ref AFTER decideApprovalAuthority returns, accepting it is post-decision and renaming it accordingly. Whichever you pick, say WHY in the plan — the next worker must not rediscover this.

DO NOT: invent a third ref, weaken DRILL C until it passes, or assert equality across a boundary the data cannot cross. And per Rail 8(B), whatever gate replaces this must assert a consumer edge, not a symbol's presence.

DOWNSTREAM: task-6646f888 waits on this row. It is one of the two genuine missing-producer problems I have been tracking since yesterday; the other, the ProductContractRevision slice, landed at commit 077376a8.

STEP 2 — MEASUREMENT CONTRADICTS THE PROPOSED ANSWER. Anchor HEAD 077376a8. Read-only; no bytes authored. Step 2 says "If your measurement contradicts this, STOP and report rather than inventing a third ref." It does. Reporting.

WHAT THE ARCHITECT GOT RIGHT. `boundHashes` is unusable pre-activation — verified in step 1 (null at reducer:90/replay:129, written only at the APPROVED transition reducer:156/replay:147, and graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:49 refuses while null). And `boundHashes.policyHash` IS an `approvalPolicyHash`: graph-transition-legs.ts:78-86 computes `approvalPolicyHash(approvalPolicyMaterial({...}))` and feeds it in as `policyHash` at :92. Both confirmed.

WHAT FAILS IS THE INVARIANT, and it fails on exactly the path this row exists to serve. The proposed answer is "compute the SAME `approvalPolicyHash` over the SAME material at plan-review time", with the checkable invariant "the value this row produces for a run must EQUAL the `boundHashes.policyHash` later written for that run's approval" — which step 5 DRILL C is instructed to assert. That material is NOT knowable at plan-review time.

`approvalPolicyMaterial` (approval-policy-digest.ts:69-82) has nine members. Seven are stable pre-activation (approvalPolicyKind, digestVersion, goalRef, graphRevisionRef, principalId, projectId, runId). TWO ARE NOT:
- `authorityDelayMs` — "the core's decided wait, never the settings' stated one" (:41)
- `grantPrincipalId` — "the human whose gate grant permitted this, or null when the policy alone permitted it" (:45)

Both come from `decideApprovalAuthority`'s verdict, and that verdict is decided AT APPROVE TIME from facts that need not exist at plan review. `packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts:127-137`:
```
const gate = request.gate;
if (gate !== null && gate !== undefined) {
  const checked = checkHumanAuthority(gate);
  if (!checked.ok) return checked;
  return Object.freeze({ delayMs: 0, grant: checked.grant, ok: true as const });
}
return decidePolicy(request.policy);   // PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN -> { delayMs: policy.delayMs, grant: null }
```
So a gated run yields `delayMs: 0, grant: <named human>` and an ungated one yields `delayMs: policy.delayMs, grant: null`. Different `grantPrincipalId`, different `authorityDelayMs`, DIFFERENT DIGEST.

And the gate can materialise between the two moments. `daemon-command-graph-approve.ts:126` calls `decideApprovalAuthority({ gate: run.gate, policy })`; when that refuses `APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and a `humanReview` witness was attached TO THE APPROVE REQUEST, `:128-130` re-derives through `operatorReviewAuthority`, which mints a grant via `grantHumanAuthority` at `request.decidedAt` (:69-79). A human review that happens after plan review therefore changes both varying members.

THAT IS THE STEP-UP PATH. A tier exists to decide whether step-up human authority is required (approval-invalidation.ts:73 special-cases R3). So the invariant holds only for runs that never needed a human — and provably breaks for every run that did. Asserting it in DRILL C would pin production to a rule production cannot honour; making it pass would mean either freezing a grant that has not happened or comparing a ref against a value nothing durably asserted, which is precisely what taskRail 1 forbids.

THE COLLISION, stated plainly. DoD 3 wants a ref that is (i) RUN-LINKED, (ii) read from durable state, (iii) not a third notion, and DoD 2 / taskRail 1 want it (iv) server-derived, never caller-supplied. At pre-activation, neither existing notion satisfies all four:
- `approvalPolicyHash` — satisfies (i)(iii)(iv), FAILS (ii) pre-activation: two of its nine members are approve-time verdicts, so any value computed now is a prediction, and it diverges exactly on the step-up path.
- `policyRevisionRef` — durable and digest-verified inside the reader (already returned as `policyRef`, reader:183), and it IS the notion the majority of production compares: recovery-completion.ts:127/:161 AND expansion-approval.ts:236 (`bound.policyDecision.policyRevisionRef`). But it FAILS (i) — the aggregate is project-scoped (`aggregateIdFor(request, null)`), so it is not run-linked — and it arguably fails (iv), since it enters the evaluation as caller-supplied `input["policyRevisionRef"]`, sealed afterwards but not server-derived in origin.

Only one of the two rail-permitted notions can be had, and each drops a different DoD clause. That is an architect decision, not a worker one, and inventing a way to satisfy both is exactly the third-notion fabrication taskRail 2 forbids.

OPTIONS, so re-planning is one hop, in my order of preference:
1. SPLIT THE ROW. The riskTier half has NO collision and is independently honest and deliverable today: project the already-digest-verified `replayed["riskAssessment"]` effective tier through the reader (step 3 as written), refusing at `DAEMON_POLICY_AUTHORITY` when the tier is ungroundable, reusing `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE`/HOLD_UNKNOWN rather than inventing a code. That unblocks the tier half of task-6646f888 now. File the policy-ref half as its own PLANNING row carrying this measurement.
2. KEEP ONE ROW, WEAKEN DoD 3's "run-linked" to `policyRevisionRef`, and say in the DoD that the plan path deliberately uses the ref the majority of consumers already compare, accepting project scope. Cheapest, but it concedes run-linkage, which the title claims.
3. KEEP `approvalPolicyHash` and REWRITE the invariant to what is actually true: the pre-activation value equals the approve-time `boundHashes.policyHash` IF AND ONLY IF the run's gate state is unchanged between the two, and a divergence must REFUSE at binding time rather than rebind. This is defensible but it is new authority design — a second materialisation point plus a divergence refusal — and it is more than step 4 as written describes.

One more thing the architect should weigh for whichever option wins: `assessRisk` sets `effectiveTier = maxTier(computedTier, input.callerRiskHint)` (policy-evaluation.ts:64-66). `callerRiskHint` is CALLER-SUPPLIED. It can only RAISE a tier and cannot ground one from null, so it cannot manufacture authority downward — but DoD 2 says a caller presenting its own riskTier is REFUSED, and the effective tier is already partly caller-influenced upstream of anything this row would build. Whether "refused" means the seam's own signature or something stricter about the hint needs saying, or step 4's refusal arm will be written against an assumption the evaluator does not hold.

Consumer edge for whichever row survives, per Rail 8(B) clause (a): task-6646f888a488481e936dc0dd3f966cd5.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED closing this as a duplicate, which was my first hypothesis. On task-6646f888 I concluded the honest source already existed via `evaluatePolicy` plus the installed policy authority. Measuring THIS row properly shows that was only two-thirds right: the evaluator exists, the decision IS durably committed, but (i) the reader never projects the tier, and (ii) `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` keys the decision project-scoped while `policyRevisionRef` enters that evaluation CALLER-SUPPLIED. Neither half is run-linked. DoD 1's adopt-and-close branch therefore does not fire, and I owe task-6646f888 an amendment so its step 3 consumes THIS source rather than reading the installed slice directly.

REJECTED `boundHashes.policyHash` as the pre-activation ref - the trap this row exists to avoid. Measured: graph-revision-reducer.ts:90 and graph-revision-replay.ts:129 set it null at creation; it is populated ONLY at the APPROVED transition (:156). At plan-review time it is null.

REJECTED inventing a third policy-ref notion, per task rail 2. `approval-policy-digest.ts` ALREADY owns the notion (APPROVAL_POLICY_DIGEST_VERSION "moe.graph.approve.policy.v1", approvalPolicyMaterial, approvalPolicyHash) and graph-transition-legs.ts:78 already computes it into policyHash. So `boundHashes.policyHash` IS an approvalPolicyHash, materialised later. The pre-activation ref is the SAME digest computed earlier - one notion, two materialisation points - which yields a checkable invariant that step 5 drills.

REJECTED building a new durable record for the tier. It is already recorded AND already recomputed and digest-verified inside the reader's own replay; it is simply not projected. Widening the projection surfaces an existing verified fact and invents no authority. That is the smallest honest change.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Measured 2026-08-29 at HEAD 62b4d7f6. Re-grep every line number.

THE TIER IS ALREADY DURABLE AND ALREADY VERIFIED, JUST NOT PROJECTED. `bootstrap-policy-services.ts` builds an evaluationInput, calls `evaluatePolicy`, and COMMITS via `commitAccepted(store, request, {aggregateId, ...})` with `authoritativeRecord = {...evaluated.record, decisionDigest}`. evaluatePolicy's returned PolicyDecisionRecord (policy-evaluation.ts:184-204) carries `riskAssessment: risk.assessment` and `policyRevisionRef`. `readPolicyEvaluationAuthority` (bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:115) then calls `evaluatedOutcome(input)`, which RE-RUNS evaluatePolicy and is checked against the stored digest - so the assessment is computed and verified inside the reader. The returned interface at :35-47 projects eleven fields and NONE of them is the tier. That single omission is the riskTier half of this row.

NOT RUN-LINKED: `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` (:61, :103) keys the decision to the project-scoped policy aggregate, and policyRevisionRef enters the evaluation as `input["policyRevisionRef"]`, i.e. caller-supplied.

THE REF NOTION ALREADY EXISTS: approval-policy-digest.ts:31 APPROVAL_POLICY_DIGEST_VERSION, :69 approvalPolicyMaterial, :86 approvalPolicyHash, documented at :7 as "a digest over the policy decision that authorised THIS approval". graph-transition-legs.ts:78 computes it and feeds it as policyHash at :92.

NEIGHBOURS TO COMPOSE, not duplicate: apps/daemon/src/planning/ already holds approval-run-binding.{ts,test.ts} (binds an approval to a run) and approval-policy-digest.ts (owns the ref notion).

CONSUMERS of readPolicyEvaluationAuthority: activation/policy-admission-reader.ts, bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts, bootstrap/bootstrap-services.test.ts. Its tests live in bootstrap-policy-authority.test.ts (there is no bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.test.ts).
planningNotes.risks:
1) WIDENING A RETURN TYPE LOOKS ADDITIVE BUT MAY NOT BE. Three production consumers read `readPolicyEvaluationAuthority`. An exactObject-style or exact-key assertion over the RETURNED object would break on a new field. Step 3 requires inspecting every call site BEFORE editing; an exact-shape consumer outside this row's roster is a split signal, not an extra path to take quietly.

2) DO NOT TOUCH ROW_KEYS OR MATERIAL_KEYS. They describe the STORED row and its material, which this row does not change. Editing either means the persisted shape moved - a much larger blast radius including the digest.

3) THE DEFAULT-VS-ABSENCE DRILL NEEDS TWO MUTATIONS. DoD 4 asks that substituting a default reds a named arm AND that substituting a DIFFERENT default reds the same arm. One mutation does not discharge it: a single default could red for the wrong reason.

4) THE POLICY-SLICE DRIFT CASE IS REAL. If a slice is reinstalled between the run's evaluation and its approval, the pre-activation ref and the later boundHashes.policyHash could disagree. The adversarial review asks what refuses in that case - it must be a refusal, never a silent mismatch.

5) A PRODUCER NOTHING IMPORTS PASSES EVERY EXISTENCE GREP. Rail 8(B) is discharged here by NAMING task-6646f888 as the consumer, since implementing that seam is explicitly out of scope for this row.

6) Bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests (root vitest include has no apps/**). Never cite it as coverage here.

7) Known foreign red: TS2353 subscriberId / EventStreamAccessConfig, peer mid-refactor in http/event-stream-access.ts. Attribute, do not fix.
